items.title: Josiah Gluck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 13, 2022
items.q: a Beethoven symphony the other day

ctx.x: Yes. I remember a buddy who would be like, he just walked into the studio like, “Well you can fix it in the mix. Oh — this is the mix? Jeez I’m sorry.” You know. It’s like — because at SNL just the culture of chops being busted sometimes is just relentless. Like, “Oh so you want it to sound like that. Okay.” You know. I mean but that’s just the nature of it. But that also happens on sessions and in situation where everybody is just really good at what they do.

I had this — I was listening to a symphony, a Beethoven symphony the other day and the balance of the instrumentation. I wonder if you’ve had the experience of recording an orchestra and then sitting with the conductor who has been responsible for the sound of the orchestra but now he wants to hear more violas. Is that even possible in that setting?

It can be, depending on what kind of forest of microphones you have put up, but typically orchestras should be recorded with as few microphones as possible. Film score recording has a much bigger forest of microphones because you may want to pick things out to help you in and around dialogue and exploding planets and spaceships or what have you.
